messages.author: 71881ca474dcdfb1
messages.subject: PNG does not render
parts:
Hi,

using the script below I can produce the image (it's saved on the
disc), but when I refresh my browser it doesn't render. Thanks in
advance for any idea.

Best, Andrej

<html>
<body>
<%
library(Cairo)
bla <- rnorm(10)
Cairo(file="/Library/WebServer/Documents/brew/plot.png", type="png")
plot(bla)
dev.off()
%>
<img src="http://localhost/brew/plot.png"/>
</body>
</html>

messages.author: 317fefd8e5bf9f73
messages.subject: Re: PNG does not render
parts:
Hi Andrej,

I also encountered read/write file permission issues in plotting that were solved by the following two steps:

--running Apache as FastCGI to resolve the permission errors, as by
http://wiki.mediatemple.net/w/Running_Apache_as_FastCGI_on_your_%28dv...

--adding apache to the psacln group and changing the group of the html and img files to psacln; as by
http://wiki.mediatemple.net/w/Working_around_permissions_issues_on_th...
(Similar to what Janno suggested I think?)

This may not apply directly to your setup but hopefully you can adjust it as necessary.  I don't know a lot about system administration so I'm not entirely sure why both steps were required...but it didn't work if I just did one or the other.  I'd also originally tried something like "sudo chmod -R 777 brew/" as you mentioned in the other thread, which seemed to change the listed permissions, but didn't change the result.

I'd double check that your image file paths are correct as well--I had some issues with mine that stumped me for quite awhile

Hope that helps,
Laura

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: PNG does not render
parts: Hi Andrej,

On Sat, Aug 28, 2010 at 4:16 PM, Andrej Kastrin
<andrej....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I hope I finally resolve the problem. The image/ directory should be
> placed outside the brew/ directory.

Good catch! and sorry I didn't see that before. While it may seem
obvious to me, not so for users learning their way around apache. To
sum up, if you use the following apache config snippet for brew:

<Directory /var/www/brew>
SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

then apache will treat all files under /var/www/brew the same way by
passing them to brew(). I remember getting tripped up by this when I
placed some javascript files under a directory served with brew. While
brew did the right thing and printed out the entire javascript file,
the content type was never set right. It would always default to
whatever DefaultType was, which in my case was either text/plain or
text/html.

Need to add this advice to the manual

Jeff

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: PNG does not render
parts:
On Mon, Aug 30, 2010 at 5:37 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Would it be possible to parse brew/R files based on their file extention
> rather than the location, like with e.g. php?

Yes, you can do that with the FilesMatch directive:

<FilesMatch "\.(brew|r|R)$">

SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew

</FilesMatch>

Place that in a <Directory> directive and that would feed any file
with a .brew, .r, or .R to brew.

More info here from the apache docs:

http://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.2/mod/core.html#filesmatch

Jeff

parts: Cool, you should add this example to the rapache manual.

On Tue, Aug 31, 2010 at 7:42 AM, Jeffrey Horner <jeffrey...@vanderbilt.edu> wrote:
On Mon, Aug 30, 2010 at 5:37 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Would it be possible to parse brew/R files based on their file extention
> rather than the location, like with e.g. php?

Yes, you can do that with the FilesMatch directive:

<FilesMatch "\.(brew|r|R)$">
      SetHandler r-script
      RHandler brew::brew
</FilesMatch>

Place that in a <Directory> directive and that would feed any file
with a .brew, .r, or .R to brew.

More info here from the apache docs:

http://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.2/mod/core.html#filesmatch

Jeff
